criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs feeds failure_section the log shape seen in the failed jobs (a shard log with no runner marker or ##[error], ending in the git credential-removal lines, 'Cleaning up orphan processes' and a '##[warning]Node.js 20' line, with the 'Post job cleanup.' header absent) and asserts the result contains none of those lines. It fails on the base tree and passes with the change; run `cargo test -p athena-core failure_section`.
criteria.evidence: The test `failure_section_drops_a_headerless_cleanup_block` builds 40 progress lines followed by a block with no header: the git `--unset-all` line, Removing HTTP extra header, Removing includeIf, Cleaning up orphan processes, and the Node.js 20 warning. It asserts none of /usr/bin/git, Removing, Cleaning up orphan, Node.js or Post job cleanup is kept. It has two variants: one without the orphan line and one with plain git lines in between. I ran the command: 11 failure_section tests passed, including the new tests for the ##[error] case, the checkout-lines case, a header on the last line, a log of only cleanup, empty output, and a log shaped like ci.yml. Base tree: Athena's revert run failed to compile, not on an assertion. From the base code shown in the diff, base cut only at the first header at or after the anchor. 'Cleaning up orphan processes' was the only header in this log, so base kept the git and Removing lines and the `!contains("/usr/bin/git")` assertion would fail. The variant without the orphan line has no header at all, so base made no cut.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs calls detail_from_job_logs with a cancelled shard whose log has only progress lines then cleanup, and asserts output_tail holds the progress lines and a note that no failing test section was found, with no cleanup text; it also asserts a shard log with a `failures:` section still keeps the test name and panicked line. Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`.
criteria.evidence: Two tests in `detail_tests` cover this. `detail_from_job_logs_notes_a_cancelled_shard_without_a_test_section` asserts every progress line is kept, the last line starts '(no failing test section was found in test (shard 3)', and no cleanup text appears. `detail_from_job_logs_keeps_the_failing_section_of_a_failed_shard` asserts failed_tests == ["athena_core tests::a"], the tail holds tests::a and 'panicked at src/lib.rs:9:5', there is no note, and there is no cleanup. Four more tests cover the note inside the line limit, the multi-unit reduction, a log stored whole, and a panic among passing units. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib detail_from_job_logs`: 6 passed. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib gh::`: 161 passed, including the existing gh/tests.rs tail tests.

criteria.criterion: A test over the stored path (with_failure_detail, plus a locally run failed check via the checks.rs run path) asserts the stored output_tail and the send_back CheckFailure tail never contain the cleanup lines, so the fix holds for every producer of a failed check record and not one job. Run `cargo test -p athena-core with_failure_detail`.
criteria.evidence: 7 tests passed. checks.rs: `with_failure_detail_drops_headerless_cleanup_from_the_stored_tail` (also checks that a second pass changes nothing) and `with_failure_detail_and_local_run_never_store_cleanup` (a real `sh` run through `run_script`). send_back.rs: `with_failure_detail_tail_is_clean_in_the_send_back` checks the CheckFailure tail, the brief, and that the note is kept. routing.rs: three end-to-end tests go through the real detail_from_job_logs, then run_routed_with_record, then CheckFailure::of and check_result_view. They cover the compile-error unit, a panic among passing units within the last 60 lines and 3000 bytes, and a cancelled shard that ends in the note.

criteria.criterion: A reading of the diff in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs shows the cleanup recognition (is_cleanup_line or a successor) lives in one function used by the local run, the reused-CI detail and the per-shard log paths; no second copy is added in gh/client.rs or send_back.rs.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, is_cleanup_header, is_cleanup_line, is_step_start, cleanup_start and CLEANUP_GAP are all defined only in checks.rs and used only by failure_section. failure_section is called by run_check (the local run), with_failure_detail, detail_from_job_logs (the per-shard path in client.rs) and CheckFailure::of. The new client.rs code (summary_units, failed_units_only) reads only `== shard` and `units failed:` lines and calls checks::has_failing_section and checks::no_test_section_note. send_back.rs adds one call to checks::failure_section. Cleanup strings appear in client.rs, send_back.rs and routing.rs only as test inputs and assertions.

criteria.criterion: The CHANGELOG.md entry names the root cause (a log with no recognised failing section fell through to a plain tail of cleanup text) and what the record stores instead, and states only what the diff does.
criteria.evidence: There is one new entry under Unreleased/Fixed. It names the failure class and the root cause: failure_section knew only runner markers and a cleanup header, so a block with no header fell through to a plain tail of cleanup text, nothing said no section was found, and the units-failed summary was never read. It describes what is stored now: the failing unit's own output, or the failing section, or the last lines before cleanup plus one note, or the cleanup-only note, and empty output unchanged. I checked its claims against the code: the walk stops at a marker or ##[error], at a ##[group]Run line, and after two plain lines in a row; the note counts inside the 200-line and byte limits; no note for a failure log kept whole; CheckFailure::of re-cuts. history.json confirms fe42b01 is the 2026-11-07 header fix. The list of recognised lines leaves out three prefixes the code knows ('Temporarily overriding HOME', 'Adding repository directory', 'Evaluate and set job outputs'). That is an omission, not a false claim.

findings.summary: The walk-back that finds the cleanup block tolerates one plain line, so a single real line after a cleanup-looking line at the end of a log is dropped.
findings.evidence: cleanup_start walks back from the end. A trailing plain line only raises `gap` to 1, which CLEANUP_GAP allows, so the walk continues to an earlier cleanup line and the cut lands above both. For a log ending 'progress / ##[warning]Node.js 20 ... / error: real failure', the stored text is 'progress' and the real error line is lost. This is found by reading the code; no test covers it. A safer rule: allow gap lines only between two cleanup lines, so the block must end in a cleanup line.

findings.summary: Athena's 'fails without the fix' runs stopped at a compile error, not a failed assertion.
findings.evidence: The fails-without-1, -2 and -3 outputs show E0425 for no_test_section_note and has_failing_section, which the new tests call. That shows the tests need the new code, but not that the behavior assertions fail on base. I established the base failure by reading the base failure_section in the diff, which cut only at a header line. If the shared helper tests had been kept separate, a run with the fix reverted would have failed on an assertion.

findings.summary: The reduction to the failing unit's output (failed_units_only) goes beyond the accepted reading's wording, though it is planned and backed by the request.
findings.evidence: The reading talks about dropping cleanup and a note for a log with no test section. The xtask summary reduction answers introspection 20261114-022748-gmm5 ('keep the failing unit's own output'), and the critic accepted it in demonstrations 2(d) and 2(f). All of it is in an expected file. It reads text that xtask prints, and the CHANGELOG states that dependency.

summary: I recommend passing this change. It fixes the problem at its source: `checks::failure_section`, the one function that picks what a failed check stores. Before, cleanup text was cut only when a recognised header line came first. Now `is_cleanup_line` recognises the cleanup lines themselves (git credential removal, Removing HTTP extra header, Node.js warnings, Complete job) and walks back from the end of the log to drop a cleanup block that has no header. A log holding only cleanup becomes a short note, and empty output stays empty. Three other changes go with it. `detail_from_job_logs` keeps the failing unit's own output and collapses the passing units to one line. A shard with no failing test section gets one final note saying so. `CheckFailure::of` cleans the stored tail again before building the send-back. The three named test commands pass in this snapshot (11, 6 and 7 tests), along with all 161 `gh::` tests and the refusal corpus. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed on this tree. Only the five expected files changed, and no admission or gate rule was touched. Two caveats. First, Athena's own "fails without the fix" runs stopped at a compile error, not a failed assertion. I showed the base failure instead by reading the base code: it cut only at a header line, so the git and Removing lines survive. Second, two minor issues: the walk-back can drop one real line that follows a cleanup line at the end of a log, and recognition only knows listed text, which the CHANGELOG states.
